summary: Run the trial CH-05 sized: split real pieces on purpose and measure what happens. What actually shipped is the half that did not need a dispatch — CH-05's one named falsifier, run and answered, plus an instrument that computes all three of Ruling C3's tripwires with the pre-split BEFORE frozen. The dispatch arm is EMPTY and this file says so first, not last.
next_step: THE OWED DISPATCH, and it is the one thing that fills the empty arm. Take one long W1 piece from NEXT-DISPATCH.md and dispatch it as TWO agents in sequence with the marker the instrument reads — the dispatch description MUST contain `chunk N of M` (e.g. "W1-33 canopy — chunk 1 of 2"), because a split that does not say so is invisible to every tripwire. Chunk 1's brief ends with: stop at ~100 requests and write orchestration/status/<PIECE>.json with findings, files_touched and a next_step naming exactly what chunk 2 picks up. Chunk 2's brief points at that file and nothing else. Run the SAME piece kind as a single marathon agent in the other arm. Then `node tools/cost.mjs --split-trial` and read the verdict: it returns UNDERPOWERED until 6 planned-split agents exist, so this needs THREE such pieces, not one. Second, smaller dispatch, and it is cheap: `--split-trial`'s tripwire 3 reads the verdict corpus directly for find-rate because no instrument computed it — that belongs in tools/scores.mjs alongside the scores, and whoever owns that file should take it.
notes: Ruling O1 followed on tools/cost.mjs: `node tools/ownership.mjs --for tools/cost.mjs` returned 'nobody live has declared this file'; the whole change was developed on a scratchpad copy and applied to the live file in ONE scripted patch run (scratchpad/split-trial/patch.mjs) with a pre-edit md5 recorded, 56529951... -> f0379211.... The patch script refuses to apply twice and refuses to apply to a file whose anchors have moved.

ONE SHARED-PATH CHANGE AND IT IS A HOIST, NOT A REWRITE. `orientationDelta` — the statistic that says what a handoff costs — was local to experimentReorientation. Q5 and Q7 must not be able to disagree about that number, and the only way to guarantee it is for there to be one function, so it moved to module scope unchanged. REGRESSION GUARD, run: --reorientation's orientation_cost and null_controls blocks are BYTE-IDENTICAL before and after ($0.4302 / -$0.0113 / -$0.0011). The only fields that moved are the ones that move on their own because the fleet kept running (the chunk-100 ceiling $2103.76 -> $2116.65 as agents accumulated, verdicts 74 -> 76).

A MISTAKE WORTH RECORDING, because it cost nothing this time and will cost somebody an hour eventually. cost.mjs derives ROOT from its own path, so a working copy under the scratchpad resolves ROOT to the scratchpad and every git call, verdict read and scores.mjs import silently misfires. I ran the dev copies from tools/ instead — and within minutes a sibling agent's bank swept `tools/cost-reverted-dev.mjs` into commit 5f669d19. It is deleted in this piece's land. A temporary file in a shared tree is a committed file; put dev copies anywhere but a directory the bank stages.
No browser needed, no GPU, no live working directory touched.
findings: WHAT I COULD NOT DO, and it is the first thing in this file rather than the last. I could not dispatch anything. No agent-spawning tool is in this agent's toolset — I searched the deferred-tool catalogue for it explicitly — and mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__create_session puts a session in a container whose transcript this box cannot read, which makes the cost measurement impossible by construction. The arms of a dispatch trial can only be filled by dispatching. So --split-trial reports planned_split = 0 across 478 subagents and returns the verdict NOT YET DISPATCHED, with every 'after' column empty BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by measurement.

SO THE PIECE DID THE HALF THAT NEEDED NO DISPATCH, AND IT IS THE HALF THAT DECIDES SOMETHING. CH-05 named exactly one falsifier: a PLANNED handoff costing MORE than an accidental one, because a deliberate status file is bigger than what a killed agent leaves behind. Nobody had run it, and it does not need a dispatch — the gradient already exists inside the accidental population, because the 53 accidental successors differ enormously in how much their predecessor had written down before it died.

THE FALSIFIER DOES NOT FIRE. Leave-behind is the bytes of the piece's orchestration/status/ files IN GIT AS OF THE SUCCESSOR'S FIRST REQUEST — not as of today, because those files have been rewritten many times since. Successors who inherited the RICHER record oriented $0.4862 CHEAPER than those who inherited the thinner one (n = 11 against 10, 2,000-draw label-shuffle p = 0.072). Nobody on this fleet inherited literally nothing, so rich-vs-none is reported as EMPTY rather than quietly swapped for the contrast that does exist.

THE CONTROL IS WHAT MAKES IT READABLE, AND IT IS THE PLAUSIBLE WRONG ANSWER RATHER THAN THE TRIVIAL ONE. A big written record belongs to a MATURE piece, and an agent on a mature piece may orient differently for reasons that have nothing to do with a handoff. So the identical measurement runs on FRESH agents — which resumed nothing — stratified by the same status-file bytes at the same dispatch times. It moves the OTHER WAY: +$0.3582 on the identical contrast (n = 26 against 23). Fresh agents on well-documented pieces orient MORE dearly, not less. The confound cannot be manufacturing the handoff arm's gradient; it is working against it. A planned split always writes the richest note there is, so the planned handoff is predicted at or BELOW the accidental $0.4302 and CH-05's $6.264 break-even is not threatened from this direction.

TWO THINGS THAT NUMBER IS NOT. p = 0.072 is not significance; it is used as a DIRECTION that survives its control, never as a size, and the log-bytes regression explains essentially nothing (R2 0.008). And it measures the SIZE of a note, never its quality — a long useless note scores the same as a short excellent one. That biases towards 'notes do not help', i.e. AGAINST the reading that makes the trial safe, which is the conservative direction and the reason it is reportable at all. Also: only 21 of the 50 matched successors could be placed on the gradient, because a description must name its piece ("Resume W1-14 r3 magic") for its status file to be findable and 29 name it only in prose ("Library r2 (successor)"). The 29 are excluded and counted, never guessed at.

DELETE-THE-FIX, EXECUTED ON A COPY, AND IT FLIPS THE SIGN. Remove the git time-travel — read each piece's status files as they are TODAY instead of as the successor found them — and the same analysis returns +$0.2767 (p = 0.370) and prints 'FALSIFIER FIRES'. The wrong implementation reaches the OPPOSITE conclusion. The mechanism is visible in the strata: today's files are 34,827 / 101,785 bytes where the successors actually inherited 14,955 / 43,171. The time-travel is load-bearing, not believed to be.

THE OTHER HALF: TWO OF CH-05'S THREE TRIPWIRES HAD NOTHING THAT COULD COMPUTE THEM. A trial whose tripwires cannot be evaluated is a trial that cannot be stopped, which is worse than not running it. `--split-trial` now computes all three, with the BEFORE frozen so a later run has something to compare against. T1 COST: $0.4302, n = 50 — the same hoisted function --reorientation uses, so the two cannot disagree. T2 SCOPE: 265 requests per unsplit piece over 28 pieces, against 1,197.5 over the 14 accidentally-split ones. T3 QUALITY: 1.30 gaps named per verdict and 1.47 separate critics per piece on unsplit pieces, against 1.52 and 3.00 on the accidental-split arm.

TRIPWIRE 2 IS BIASED AGAINST FIRING AND THAT IS THE RIGHT DIRECTION, said on the tripwire itself rather than in a footnote: a piece is split BECAUSE it is long, so a split piece's total starts above the median for reasons that have nothing to do with the change. A tripwire 2 that fires despite that bias has found a real loss of work; a quiet one has proved less than it looks. Read it as 'no alarm', never as 'scope preserved'.

SELF-TEST: five synthetic fleets whose right answers differ, and TWO OF THEM ARE REFUSAL TRAPS rather than wrong answers — which is the shape this instrument needed, because its live input has an empty arm. Arm Q (a 60-request runway) is detected at the hand-computable $2.64 (5.28 Mtok x $0.50/Mtok) and returns REVERT; arm P returns CONTINUE, so the arms genuinely disagree. Arm R cuts the work to a quarter and fires TRIPWIRE 2 while tripwire 1 stays quiet, proving the two catch different failures. Arm N feeds the SAME $2.64 handoff on only 2 agents and must return UNDERPOWERED — not revert, not continue. Arm E has no planned splits at all, the live case, and must return NOT YET DISPATCHED with an empty after column. 9 of 9 arms pass, and both cost --self-test and --experiments-self-test are green on the live file.

WHAT THE SELF-TEST DOES NOT COVER, stated rather than glossed: tripwire 3 reads the real verdict corpus from disk inside the experiment, so no synthetic arm exercises its find-rate arithmetic — only the live corpus does. Whoever moves find-rate into tools/scores.mjs (see next_step) should give it a fixture there.

THE MARKER IS EXPLICIT AND THE NEXT DISPATCH MUST USE IT. A planned split is recognised only by `chunk N`, `part N of M` or `split N/M` in the dispatch description, exactly as RESUMED_RE demands explicit resume markers. A regex that guessed would fold ordinary round-2 dispatches into the planned arm and manufacture the very population this piece reports as absent — and the instrument would then be measuring its own idea of a split instead of a real one.
